south-africa/waterfront.name: V&A Waterfront
south-africa/waterfront.description: Cape Town's working harbour turned visitor district, with shops, restaurants, an aquarium and views of Table Mountain.
south-africa/waterfront.details: The V&A Waterfront is a former dock area that blends shops, restaurants and entertainment with a working harbour, with Table Mountain as a backdrop. It holds the Two Oceans Aquarium, the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa in a converted grain silo, and the ferry terminal for Robben Island. Seals often rest on the quay. It is busy and safe by city standards, a convenient first stop after arrival.

south-africa/table-mountain.name: Table Mountain
south-africa/table-mountain.description: The flat-topped mountain above Cape Town, reached by rotating cable car or a steep hike, with views over the city and sea.
south-africa/table-mountain.details: Table Mountain rises about 1,085 metres above the city and is the defining landmark of Cape Town. A cable car with a rotating floor climbs to the summit in a few minutes, and there are hiking routes up for the fit, the Platteklip Gorge route being the most direct and steep. The cable car stops running in strong wind or when cloud covers the top, so check conditions on the day. Buying tickets online saves queueing, and a warm layer is useful at the top.

south-africa/robben-island.name: Robben Island
south-africa/robben-island.description: The island prison where Nelson Mandela spent many years, visited by ferry from the waterfront.
south-africa/robben-island.details: Robben Island was used as a prison for political detainees during the apartheid era, and Nelson Mandela spent eighteen of his twenty-seven years in custody here. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and tours are guided, in many cases by former prisoners, taking in the cells and the lime quarry. The trip takes about three and a half hours including the ferry, which is cancelled in rough seas. Tickets sell out well ahead in season.

south-africa/bo-kaap.name: Bo-Kaap
south-africa/bo-kaap.description: A hillside neighbourhood of brightly painted houses and cobbled streets, the historic home of Cape Town's Cape Malay community.
south-africa/bo-kaap.details: Bo-Kaap sits on the slope of Signal Hill above the city centre, known for rows of houses painted in strong pinks, greens and blues. It has been home to the Cape Malay community, descended from enslaved and exiled people brought from Southeast Asia, since the eighteenth century, and has several old mosques and a small museum. It is a living neighbourhood, so be respectful about photographing residents. Cape Malay cooking is a speciality, with spiced curries and sweet koesisters.

south-africa/camps-bay-sunset.name: Camps Bay sunset
south-africa/camps-bay-sunset.description: A palm-lined beach promenade on the Atlantic seaboard backed by the Twelve Apostles, popular for sunset drinks.
south-africa/camps-bay-sunset.details: Camps Bay is a white-sand beach at the foot of the Twelve Apostles mountain range, with a strip of cafes and bars along the road behind it. It is the classic place for a sunset drink, and the light on the mountains is excellent. The Atlantic water is very cold, and in summer the strong south-easter wind can blow sand along the beach. It is a short drive from the city centre.

south-africa/kirstenbosch.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
south-africa/kirstenbosch.description: A botanical garden on the slopes of Table Mountain showing the region's fynbos plants, with a treetop walkway.
south-africa/kirstenbosch.details: Kirstenbosch was established in 1913 and displays plants from across southern Africa on the eastern flank of Table Mountain, including the fynbos vegetation that makes the Cape floral region so distinctive. A curved treetop walkway called the Boomslang rises among the canopy of the arboretum. In summer, Sunday-evening concerts are held on the lawn. Paths slope gently, and a shuttle carries visitors around the garden.

south-africa/lions-head.name: Lion's Head hike
south-africa/lions-head.description: A popular sunrise or sunset walk up a peak beside Table Mountain, finishing with chains and ladders.
south-africa/lions-head.details: Lion's Head is a 669-metre peak between Table Mountain and the sea, with a spiralling path that gives a view over the city, the Atlantic coast and the mountain. The last section includes chains and ladders and needs a steady head. It takes about two hours return and is especially popular around sunrise and at full moon. Start with a head torch if going in the dark, and go in company.

south-africa/cape-point.name: Cape Point and the Cape of Good Hope
south-africa/cape-point.description: A nature reserve at the tip of the Cape Peninsula, with a lighthouse, funicular and dramatic cliffs.
south-africa/cape-point.details: Cape Point lies at the southern end of the Cape Peninsula in the Cape of Good Hope Nature Reserve. A funicular and a short path climb to the old lighthouse, with views along the cliffs to the Atlantic and Indian oceans. The reserve also has baboons, which will steal food, so do not feed them and keep bags closed. The drive from Cape Town often follows Chapman's Peak Drive, a coastal road that closes at times for rockfalls or high winds.

south-africa/boulders-penguins.name: Boulders Beach penguins
south-africa/boulders-penguins.description: A sheltered cove near Simon's Town where a colony of African penguins nests and swims.
south-africa/boulders-penguins.details: Boulders Beach is a sheltered cove among granite boulders, where African penguins settled in the 1980s and now number in the thousands. Boardwalks lead through the colony, and a small beach lets visitors swim in the same waters. The birds are endangered and can bite, so keep your distance. It is best in the morning, before the tour buses arrive.

south-africa/stellenbosch-wine-estates.name: Stellenbosch wine estates
south-africa/stellenbosch-wine-estates.description: A day of tastings at wine farms in the valleys around Stellenbosch, many with Cape Dutch buildings and mountain views.
south-africa/stellenbosch-wine-estates.details: The Stellenbosch region holds dozens of wine estates producing reds such as cabernet sauvignon and pinotage, a grape developed in the area in the 1920s, along with chenin blanc and other whites. Tasting rooms often sit in Cape Dutch farm buildings with gardens and mountain views, and many serve lunch. Plan two or three estates rather than more, and arrange a driver or a tour so that no one has to drive after tasting.

south-africa/stellenbosch-town.name: Stellenbosch town walk
south-africa/stellenbosch-town.description: A walk through South Africa's second-oldest town, with oak-lined streets, Cape Dutch houses and a university.
south-africa/stellenbosch-town.details: Stellenbosch was founded in 1679 and has some of the best-preserved Cape Dutch architecture in the country, white-gabled houses lining oak-shaded streets. The Village Museum on Ryneveld Street is made up of several historic houses. The university gives the town a youthful feel, with cafes and galleries around Dorp Street. It is flat and easy to explore on foot.

south-africa/franschhoek.name: Franschhoek
south-africa/franschhoek.description: A valley village settled by French Huguenots, known for its restaurants and a hop-on hop-off wine tram.
south-africa/franschhoek.details: Franschhoek, meaning French corner, was settled in the late seventeenth century by Huguenot refugees who brought winemaking skills, and the name is still seen in the estates around it. It has a reputation for some of the best restaurants in the Cape, set against a ring of mountains. A hop-on hop-off wine tram links several estates, and booking ahead is wise. The village is compact and walkable.

south-africa/bettys-bay-penguins.name: Stony Point penguin colony
south-africa/bettys-bay-penguins.description: A small breeding colony of African penguins and cormorants on the coast at Betty's Bay.
south-africa/bettys-bay-penguins.details: Stony Point is a nature reserve on the False Bay coast where African penguins breed among the ruins of an old whaling station, viewed from a short boardwalk. It is quieter and less commercial than the Boulders colony near Cape Town. Birds can be seen moulting or nesting, depending on the season. The nearby Clarence Drive is a scenic coastal road that makes a good approach.

south-africa/hermanus-cliff-path.name: Hermanus Cliff Path and whale watching
south-africa/hermanus-cliff-path.description: A coastal walking path above the bay where southern right whales can be watched from the shore in season.
south-africa/hermanus-cliff-path.details: Hermanus is one of the best places in the world to watch whales from land, as southern right whales come into the bay to calve between roughly June and November, peaking in September and October. The Cliff Path runs along the shore for about twelve kilometres with benches and viewpoints, and the town even has a whale crier who blows a kelp horn to announce sightings. Outside the whale season the walk is still a pleasant coastal stroll. The path has some steps and uneven stretches.

south-africa/hemel-en-aarde.name: Hemel-en-Aarde wine valley
south-africa/hemel-en-aarde.description: A cool-climate wine valley near Hermanus known for pinot noir and chardonnay, with tastings and views.
south-africa/hemel-en-aarde.details: The Hemel-en-Aarde valley, meaning heaven and earth, is a cool-climate wine area close to the Atlantic that produces some of the country's best pinot noir and chardonnay. Its estates are smaller and quieter than those around Stellenbosch, with tasting rooms looking over vineyards. Tastings may need to be booked ahead, and as ever a designated driver is essential.

south-africa/oudtshoorn-ostrich-farm.name: Ostrich farm visit
south-africa/oudtshoorn-ostrich-farm.description: A guided visit to an ostrich farm in the Little Karoo, where birds are fed and the industry's history is explained.
south-africa/oudtshoorn-ostrich-farm.details: Oudtshoorn grew rich on ostrich feathers in the early twentieth century, and farms around the town still raise the birds for meat, leather and feathers. Guided tours explain the life cycle, show eggs and chicks and usually let visitors feed the ostriches. Some farms offer rides, which raise animal welfare questions, so many travellers skip them. Mornings are cooler for a visit.

south-africa/cango-caves.name: Cango Caves
south-africa/cango-caves.description: A limestone cave system north of Oudtshoorn with large chambers and, for the adventurous, tight crawling passages.
south-africa/cango-caves.details: The Cango Caves are a series of vast limestone chambers with stalactites and stalagmites, reached by guided tour. The standard heritage tour covers the large halls, while the adventure tour goes through narrow passages and squeezes that can be very tight, so it is not for anyone claustrophobic or large-framed. Temperatures are steady and cool. Tours run at set times, so check them on arrival.

south-africa/knysna-lagoon.name: Knysna Lagoon and the Heads
south-africa/knysna-lagoon.description: A tidal lagoon ringed by forest, guarded at its mouth by two sandstone cliffs known as the Knysna Heads.
south-africa/knysna-lagoon.details: Knysna sits on a large lagoon that meets the Indian Ocean through a narrow channel flanked by the high sandstone cliffs called the Heads. Viewpoints on the eastern head look over the entrance, and boat cruises run on the lagoon. The town is known for its oysters, eaten fresh at waterfront restaurants. The forests behind are part of the Garden Route and home to Knysna's rare forest elephants, which are almost never seen.

south-africa/robberg.name: Robberg Nature Reserve
south-africa/robberg.description: A rocky peninsula near Plettenberg Bay with coastal hiking trails and a colony of Cape fur seals.
south-africa/robberg.details: Robberg is a narrow peninsula reaching into the Indian Ocean, with trails of varying lengths from about two to five hours, passing dunes, cliffs and a seal colony at the tip. It is a UNESCO-listed heritage site, and whales and dolphins can sometimes be seen from the path. The trail includes steep sand dunes and rocky sections, and wind can be strong. Take water and sun protection.

south-africa/tsitsikamma.name: Tsitsikamma and the Storms River Mouth
south-africa/tsitsikamma.description: A coastal forest park with a suspension bridge over the Storms River mouth and trails along the shore.
south-africa/tsitsikamma.details: Tsitsikamma National Park protects a rugged strip of forest and rocky coast on the Garden Route. At the Storms River Mouth a short trail leads to a suspension bridge across the river as it meets the sea, with longer paths along the coast. Spray and waves make the rocks slippery. It is a fairly short walk and suits most fitness levels, though stairs are involved.

south-africa/addo-elephant-park.name: Addo Elephant National Park
south-africa/addo-elephant-park.description: A malaria-free park near Port Elizabeth with several hundred elephants and the Big Five.
south-africa/addo-elephant-park.details: Addo was created in the 1930s to protect a tiny remnant population of elephants and now holds several hundred of them, along with lions, buffalo, rhino and leopard, so that all of the Big Five are present. It is free of malaria, which suits families and those who prefer not to take medication. Visitors can self-drive on its roads or take guided game drives, which tend to find more. Early morning and late afternoon give the best viewing.

south-africa/kruger-morning-drive.name: Dawn game drive in the Kruger area
south-africa/kruger-morning-drive.description: An open-vehicle drive at first light with a ranger, the time when predators and other animals are most active.
south-africa/kruger-morning-drive.details: Kruger National Park and the private reserves beside it are home to the Big Five and many other species, and the most productive time to see them is dawn, when it is cool and animals are active. A ranger drives and tracks in an open vehicle, with a spotter, and explains what you see. Warm clothes are needed even in a hot season. Sightings are never guaranteed but are often outstanding. The Kruger area is a malaria-risk region, so seek medical advice before travelling.

south-africa/kruger-evening-drive.name: Evening game drive and sundowner
south-africa/kruger-evening-drive.description: An afternoon drive in the bush that ends with drinks as the sun sets, then a short night drive back.
south-africa/kruger-evening-drive.details: The late-afternoon drive follows animals as they emerge in the cooler hours, usually stopping at a viewpoint for a sundowner, drinks and snacks at sunset. On the way back, rangers use a spotlight to look for nocturnal animals such as leopards, civets and owls. It is cool after dark, so bring a jacket. Insect repellent is important in the evenings.

south-africa/kruger-bush-walk.name: Guided bush walk
south-africa/kruger-bush-walk.description: A walk through the bush with an armed ranger, learning to read tracks, plants and insects rather than seeing the big animals from a vehicle.
south-africa/kruger-bush-walk.details: On a guided walking safari, a trained, armed ranger leads a small group on foot, stopping to explain tracks, dung, trees and insects and reading signs that are missed from a vehicle. Big animals may be encountered, and the ranger gives clear instructions on what to do. Walks are early in the morning and last a few hours. They are not allowed for young children, and the pace is slow.

south-africa/blyde-river-canyon.name: Blyde River Canyon and the Three Rondavels
south-africa/blyde-river-canyon.description: One of the largest green canyons in the world, with sheer cliffs and three rounded rock peaks above a reservoir.
south-africa/blyde-river-canyon.details: The Blyde River Canyon is a huge, vegetated gorge in Mpumalanga, about twenty-five kilometres long and reaching depths of up to a kilometre. The Three Rondavels, a trio of round-topped rock peaks, are the best-known viewpoint, looking down to the Blyde River Dam. Mist often covers the escarpment, so views vary greatly, and early morning is usually clearest. Paths between the lookouts are short and paved.

south-africa/gods-window.name: God's Window and Lisbon Falls
south-africa/gods-window.description: A clifftop viewpoint over the Lowveld plain on the Panorama Route, close to a series of waterfalls.
south-africa/gods-window.details: God's Window is a lookout on the edge of the Drakensberg escarpment from which the land drops about 900 metres to the Lowveld, with Kruger visible far away on a clear day. It is often covered in cloud, in which case it is worth waiting. A short stepped path climbs to a higher viewpoint. Nearby waterfalls such as Lisbon Falls can be reached on short walks.

south-africa/bourkes-luck-potholes.name: Bourke's Luck Potholes
south-africa/bourkes-luck-potholes.description: Cylindrical holes worn into the rock where the Treur and Blyde rivers meet, crossed by footbridges.
south-africa/bourkes-luck-potholes.details: At Bourke's Luck, swirling water has ground deep, smooth cylindrical potholes into the rock over millions of years, at the meeting of the Treur and Blyde rivers. A series of footbridges and paths lead across and around them. It is a short and easy stop on the Panorama Route and best in the morning light. The rock is wet and slippery near the water.

south-africa/apartheid-museum.name: Apartheid Museum
south-africa/apartheid-museum.description: A museum in Johannesburg tracing the rise and fall of apartheid through film, photographs and personal stories.
south-africa/apartheid-museum.details: The Apartheid Museum opened in 2001 and tells the story of segregation and the struggle against it through archive film, photographs, documents and personal testimony. Visitors enter through separate gates marked for white and non-white people, a stark start to the exhibits. Allow at least two to three hours; some images are upsetting. It is a quiet, reflective place and a good first stop in Johannesburg.

south-africa/soweto-tour.name: Soweto tour
south-africa/soweto-tour.description: A guided visit to Johannesburg's best-known township, with Vilakazi Street and the Hector Pieterson Memorial.
south-africa/soweto-tour.details: Soweto is a large township south-west of central Johannesburg that played a central role in the anti-apartheid struggle. Guided tours usually include Vilakazi Street, once home to both Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu, and the Hector Pieterson Memorial, which marks the 1976 student uprising. Local guides give much better context than a self-drive, and a visit often includes a meal in a family-run restaurant. Go with a reputable operator.

south-africa.name: South Africa
south-africa.description: A country of Big Five safaris, vineyards, dramatic coasts and the city of Cape Town beneath Table Mountain.

south-africa/western-cape.name: Western Cape
south-africa/western-cape.description: The south-western province that holds Cape Town, the Winelands, Hermanus and the Garden Route.

south-africa/cape-town.name: Cape Town
south-africa/cape-town.description: A harbour city beneath Table Mountain, with beaches, vineyards, a penguin colony and the Cape Peninsula close by.

south-africa/cape-point.name: Cape Point
south-africa/cape-point.description: The cliff-edged tip of the Cape Peninsula within the Cape of Good Hope Nature Reserve.

south-africa/stellenbosch.name: Stellenbosch
south-africa/stellenbosch.description: The Cape's oldest wine town, with oak-lined streets, Cape Dutch houses and many wine estates close by.

south-africa/franschhoek.name: Franschhoek
south-africa/franschhoek.description: A valley village settled by French Huguenots, known for its restaurants and wine estates.

south-africa/hermanus.name: Hermanus
south-africa/hermanus.description: A seaside town and one of the world's best places to watch southern right whales from the shore.

south-africa/oudtshoorn.name: Oudtshoorn
south-africa/oudtshoorn.description: The ostrich capital of the Little Karoo, close to the Cango Caves and reached by Route 62.

south-africa/knysna.name: Knysna
south-africa/knysna.description: A Garden Route town on a forest-ringed lagoon, known for oysters and the sandstone Knysna Heads.

south-africa/plettenberg-bay.name: Plettenberg Bay
south-africa/plettenberg-bay.description: A beach resort on the Garden Route, close to the Robberg Nature Reserve with its seal colony.

south-africa/tsitsikamma.name: Tsitsikamma
south-africa/tsitsikamma.description: A coastal forest and rocky shoreline on the Garden Route, with a suspension bridge at the Storms River Mouth.

south-africa/eastern-cape.name: Eastern Cape
south-africa/eastern-cape.description: The province east of the Garden Route, with the malaria-free Addo Elephant National Park near Port Elizabeth.

south-africa/addo.name: Addo
south-africa/addo.description: The area around Addo Elephant National Park, a malaria-free safari destination near Port Elizabeth.

south-africa/mpumalanga.name: Mpumalanga
south-africa/mpumalanga.description: The north-eastern province of the Panorama Route and the southern part of Kruger National Park.

south-africa/kruger-national-park.name: Kruger National Park
south-africa/kruger-national-park.description: South Africa's flagship safari park, home to the Big Five and best seen in the dry winter months.

south-africa/graskop.name: Graskop
south-africa/graskop.description: A small town on the Panorama Route, close to Blyde River Canyon, God's Window and several waterfalls.

south-africa/gauteng.name: Gauteng
south-africa/gauteng.description: South Africa's smallest and most urban province, home to Johannesburg and Pretoria.

south-africa/johannesburg.name: Johannesburg
south-africa/johannesburg.description: South Africa's largest city and main international gateway, with powerful apartheid-era history and the township of Soweto.
